title: Print message
description: Print text with predictable formatting.
explanation: Print text with predictable formatting.
usage: Use this when you need to print text with predictable formatting.
mistakes: Use printf with a fixed format string instead of interpolating text into the format.

title: Variable
description: Assign and read a shell variable.
explanation: Assign and read a shell variable.
usage: Use this when you need to assign and read a shell variable.
mistakes: Assignments have no spaces around =; quote expansions when reading the value.

title: Arguments
description: Read an optional first command-line argument.
explanation: Read an optional first command-line argument.
usage: Use this when you need to read an optional first command-line argument.
output: Hello, friend! (when no argument is supplied)
mistakes: Use ${1:-default} when strict mode may encounter a missing argument.

title: Read input
description: Read a line without interpreting backslashes.
explanation: Read a line without interpreting backslashes.
usage: Use this when you need to read a line without interpreting backslashes.
mistakes: read -r preserves backslashes instead of interpreting them.

title: File condition
description: Check whether a regular file exists.
explanation: Check whether a regular file exists.
usage: Use this when you need to check whether a regular file exists.
mistakes: Quote filenames even inside a test for consistent habits.

title: Directory condition
description: Check whether a directory exists.
explanation: Check whether a directory exists.
usage: Use this when you need to check whether a directory exists.
mistakes: -d checks for a directory, while -f checks a regular file.

title: String comparison
description: Compare two strings.
explanation: Compare two strings.
usage: Use this when you need to compare two strings.
mistakes: [[ ]] uses Bash syntax and is not portable to plain sh.

title: Numeric comparison
code:
score=82
if (( score >= 60 )); then
  printf 'Passed\n'
fi
description: Compare integers with arithmetic syntax.
explanation: Compare integers with arithmetic syntax.
usage: Use this when you need to compare integers with arithmetic syntax.
mistakes: Arithmetic contexts do not use string comparison operators.

title: For loop
code:
for item in HTML CSS Python; do
  printf '%s\n' "$item"
done
description: Visit each item in a list.
explanation: Visit each item in a list.
usage: Use this when you need to visit each item in a list.
mistakes: Quote expansions if your list comes from variables instead of literal words.

title: While loop
code:
count=0
while (( count < 3 )); do
  printf '%s\n' "$count"
  count=$((count + 1))
done
description: Repeat until an integer limit is reached.
explanation: Repeat until an integer limit is reached.
usage: Use this when you need to repeat until an integer limit is reached.
mistakes: Under set -e, ((count++)) can exit when the expression evaluates to zero; assignment avoids that.

title: Array
description: Store and expand multiple values safely.
explanation: Store and expand multiple values safely.
usage: Use this when you need to store and expand multiple values safely.
mistakes: Use "${items[@]}" to preserve each array element as one argument.

title: Function
description: Group a reusable shell action.
explanation: Group a reusable shell action.
usage: Use this when you need to group a reusable shell action.
mistakes: local limits variable scope to the function.

title: Make directory
description: Create a nested directory if missing.
explanation: Create a nested directory if missing.
usage: Use this when you need to create a nested directory if missing.
mistakes: The -p option handles existing parent directories.

title: Copy file
description: Copy a file without overwriting a backup.
explanation: Copy a file without overwriting a backup.
usage: Use this when you need to copy a file without overwriting a backup.
mistakes: cp -n behavior can differ by implementation; this example refuses replacement.

title: Read file
code:
if [[ -f "notes.txt" ]]; then
  while IFS= read -r line || [[ -n "$line" ]]; do
    printf '%s\n' "$line"
  done < "notes.txt"
fi
description: Read lines while preserving whitespace.
explanation: Read lines while preserving whitespace.
usage: Use this when you need to read lines while preserving whitespace.
mistakes: The final || check preserves a last line without a newline.

title: Write file
description: Write text to a file, replacing its contents.
explanation: Write text to a file, replacing its contents.
usage: Use this when you need to write text to a file, replacing its contents.
mistakes: The > operator replaces an existing file.

title: Append file
description: Add a line to the end of a file.
explanation: Add a line to the end of a file.
usage: Use this when you need to add a line to the end of a file.
mistakes: The >> operator appends instead of replacing.

title: Pipe sort
code: printf '%s\n' CSS HTML CSS | sort | uniq
description: Chain commands to sort and remove duplicates.
explanation: Chain commands to sort and remove duplicates.
usage: Use this when you need to chain commands to sort and remove duplicates.
mistakes: uniq only removes adjacent duplicate lines, so sort first.

title: Grep search
description: Find lines containing literal text.
explanation: Find lines containing literal text.
usage: Use this when you need to find lines containing literal text.
mistakes: grep exits with 1 when no line matches; handle that under strict mode.

title: Command substitution
description: Capture a command output in a variable.
explanation: Capture a command output in a variable.
usage: Use this when you need to capture a command output in a variable.
mistakes: Command substitution removes trailing newlines from the captured output.

title: Exit status
code:
if command -v git >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  printf 'Git is available\n'
else
  printf 'Git is missing\n' >&2
fi
description: Check a command’s success directly.
explanation: Check a command’s success directly.
usage: Use this when you need to check a command’s success directly.
mistakes: Check the command directly instead of relying on a stale $?.

title: Case menu
description: Dispatch among named command choices.
explanation: Dispatch among named command choices.
usage: Use this when you need to dispatch among named command choices.
output: Usage: bash main.sh start (without an argument)
mistakes: Each case arm ends with ;; and the block ends with esac.

title: Temporary file
code:
temp_file="$(mktemp)"
trap 'rm -f -- "$temp_file"' EXIT
printf 'Temporary data\n' > "$temp_file"
cat -- "$temp_file"
description: Create a temporary file and clean it on exit.
explanation: Create a temporary file and clean it on exit.
usage: Use this when you need to create a temporary file and clean it on exit.
mistakes: Keep the trap single-quoted so the temporary filename expands when it runs.

title: Find files
description: List matching text files without unsafe splitting.
explanation: List matching text files without unsafe splitting.
usage: Use this when you need to list matching text files without unsafe splitting.
mistakes: Do not parse find output with a whitespace-splitting for loop.

title: Environment default
description: Allow environment configuration with a default.
explanation: Allow environment configuration with a default.
usage: Use this when you need to allow environment configuration with a default.
mistakes: An unset or empty OUTPUT_DIR uses the fallback here.

title: Validate argument
code:
if [[ $# -eq 0 ]]; then
  printf 'Provide an argument\n' >&2
  exit 1
fi
printf 'Argument: %s\n' "$1"
description: Reject missing required arguments.
explanation: Reject missing required arguments.
usage: Use this when you need to reject missing required arguments.
mistakes: With set -u, verify an argument exists before reading $1.

title: Complete backup script
code:
source_file="${1:-notes.txt}"
if [[ ! -f "$source_file" ]]; then
  printf 'File not found: %s\n' "$source_file" >&2
  exit 1
fi
mkdir -p -- backups
cp -n -- "$source_file" "backups/$(basename -- "$source_file").bak"
printf 'Backup complete\n'
description: Back up a chosen file without replacing an existing backup.
explanation: Back up a chosen file without replacing an existing backup.
usage: Use this when you need to back up a chosen file without replacing an existing backup.
output: Backup complete (when the source file exists)
mistakes: Quote paths and avoid overwriting backups; this example writes into backups/.
